events.headline: SpaceX catches Starship’s top section on return to Texas launch tower
events.summary: SpaceX’s Starship spacecraft returned to its launch site in Boca Chica, Texas, after a 22‑hour orbital flight and was caught by the tower’s mechanical arms on 15 November. The top section was secured, while the bottom booster exploded after an aborted recovery attempt.
events.whyItMatters: Recovering Starship’s parts is key to making the rocket reusable, which could lower launch costs and support NASA’s Artemis moon missions.

deeper.background: SpaceX has been testing its massive Starship system for years, aiming to make both the spacecraft and its booster fully reusable. This test was the 15th flight and the first successful capture of the spacecraft’s top section.
deeper.whatNext: SpaceX plans to begin launching Starship from Florida’s Kennedy Space Center in the coming months and will continue attempts to recover the booster stage.

deeper.simpler: SpaceX sent a huge rocket into space, brought it back, and used big robot arms to grab the top part. The bottom part blew up, but catching the top is a step toward reusing rockets.

events.summary: US negotiators have raised the idea of Ukraine withdrawing its remaining forces from the eastern Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. events.summary: A Copa Airlines passenger jet and a UPS cargo plane collided on a taxiway at Miami International Airport on Saturday night, resulting in minor injuries for two people. events.headline: Italy fines Meta €805 million over unauthorized photo gallery access
events.summary: Italy's data protection agency imposed an €805 million fine on Meta for accessing Android users' photos and videos without proper consent or adequate notice. The regulator stated that the Facebook app's gallery suggestions feature failed to clearly inform users that granting app-wide access would allow photo-based post suggestions. Meta was given 60 days to disable the feature by default and stated its intention to appeal the decision.
events.whyItMatters: This financial penalty is among the largest ever imposed by Italian authorities on a technology company, signaling strict enforcement of data privacy regulations for big tech platforms operating in Europe.
